analytic.title: Fault-Tolerant Scheduling of Primary-Alternate Version Based on Variable Workload

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: Task workload analysis for primary-alternate fault- tolerance is usually performed based on WCET (Worst-Case Execution Time), which causes excessive redundancy of processor resource reservation in conventional real-time systems. To address this issue, a novel primary-alternate faulttolerant model based on a variable workload is built, theorems for both the alternate version's schedulability and the primary version's execution success ratio is proposed, and their correctness are proved. Motivated by these theorems, a new algorithm called BCEVW (BCE with Variable Workload) is proposed through improving the algorithm BCE(Basic, CAT, EIT). Further, a new error probability model for the primary version is proposed, which is closer to the practice than does the conventional model. Using two metrics including schedulability of a task set and execution success ratio of the primary version, simulation results show that (1) for scheduling task sets in the alternate version, backwards-EDF algorithm performs better than backwards-RM algorithm, and the necessary and sufficient conditions for its schedulability is that the processor utilization is no more than 1; (2) in the case of variable workload, BCEVW algorithm can significantly improve the schedulability of task sets in the primary version;

(3) for the new error probability model, the results of the proposed scheduling algorithm show that there is an obvious linear relationship between the error probability and execution success ratio of the primary version, and further the greater processor utilization of the primary version is, the more significant linear relationship is.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: Hard real-time systems used in safety-critical applications should not only ensure real-time tasks deadline, but also ensure real-time tasks to be executed correctly when systems encounter faults. In order to increase the throughput and reliability of a hard real-time system on the basis of ensuring temporality, the fault-tolerant technology research is needed urgently. Software fault-tolerance of real-time systems is an important branch of study, and its main idea is to do fault-tolerance by redundancy of multiple versions of a program. Campbell et al. first proposed the use of faulttolerant mechanism of the primary version and redundant alternate version of the program to solve software problems. The primary version of the program is capable of providing high-quality output, but its complexity of program results in a higher probability of errors, and the alternate version provides an acceptable output without errors after full validation runs [1] . Chetto etc. proposed EDL (Earliest-Deadline-first as Late as possible) algorithm that reserve time beforehand for the alternate version in an on-line manner, the alternate version will be dropped if the primary version is executed successfully, and further the EDL algorithm is used to adjust the alternate version of scheduled time table [2] . Han etc. further proposed BCE (Basic, CAT, EIT) algorithm introducing CAT (Checking Available Time) and EIT (Eliminating Idle Time) strategies in the basis of Basic algorithm to improve the execution success ratio of task primary version and to reduce processor time wasted due to the failure of primary version [3] . Liu et al. proposed DPA and EDPA algorithms to improve Han's CAT algorithm by constructing prediction table to improve the predictability of the primary version [4] . In recent years, a number of researchers have studied the problems of fault-tolerance in mixed-criticality systems, and they mostly introduced and improved scheduling algorithms of systems at low and high two criticality level [12][13][14][15][16] . Although the mixed-criticality systems are assumed that the workload of system is different in low and criticality mode, but their workloads are still assumed to be equal to WCET, and the inherent problems of workload variability of job in a different criticality levels of task were not analyzed. In addition, these studies tend to assume simple model about software errors, and lack indepth research on the error probability model [1][2][3][4] .

The above research efforts assume the task execution time equal to WCET as constant, which simplifies performance analysis model, but over-pessimistically analyzes the performance of real-time systems, since the demand for the implementation of worst-case is almost impossible in actual operation [5] , therefore, scheduling policy based on the WCET, such as RMS (Rate-Monotonic Scheduling) [6] lead to a lot of time remaining, and the surplus computing resources can be used to improve schedulability of the task set and fault-tolerance of real-time systems. Based on this, a number of researchers have studied variable workload, the literature [7-10] proposed the use of a random variable to denote the task execution time, but it can't be used in hard real-time systems due to missed deadlines, and literature [11] further proposed modeling method of variable execution demand in which different resource consumption models are used for different tasks. In particular, Maxiaguine et al. propose to adopt workload curve to describe variable workload. Comparing to stochastic simulation methods, this modeling method not only can guarantee hard real-time performance, but also can break the restriction for WCET-based analysis by introducing the model of variable workload [12] . Based on above research, in order to trade the quality of computation results for redundancy of WCET analysis and software fault tolerance, this paper introduces the software fault-tolerant technology into the variable workload model, and sets workload to be a variable in fault-tolerant scheduling analysis to study the use of idle time of processor to improve the execution success ratio of the primary version. Further, on the basis of the proposed task error probability model, it analyzes and optimizes primary-alternate faulttolerant scheduling strategies, which not only ensures to meet deadlines of hard real-time tasks, but also improves the schedulability of the primary version of task sets. 2) The basic agreement a) = , task period equals its relative deadline. b) , = , -1 + , and the first release time of task equals zero, therefore,〈 , , , , 〉 can be rewritten as 4-tuple〈 , , , 〉.

div.head: C. fault-tolerant model of primary-alternate with variable workload
div.p: In conventional software fault-tolerant model of primaryalternate, task execution time is assumed to equal WCET, it pessimistically estimates processor computing resources, and thus results in system design excessive redundancy. The worst-case execution time is almost impossible to happen in the actual system running process, so task scheduling model based on WCET can incur two problems as follow:
First, the too much reserved resources of system result in waste of resources;

Second, the task set scheduling estimates are pessimistic, e.g., the task set could have been ran correctly, but pessimistic estimates result task set can't be scheduled; system could perform more primary, but pessimism estimates cause decreasing numbers of primary, and result in less precise output of job.

In conventional periodic task fault-tolerant model of primary-alternate, the execution time of primary and alternate are assumed to be constant p i and a i respectively, and pessimistic are assumed to equal to the worst-case execution time. Based on variable workload theory, we improve the conventional model: the main idea is p i and a i should be variables in each cycle j for each task, i.e., the periodic 4-tuple should be changed to〈T i , D i , p i (j), a i (j)〉 k ∈ ℤ > 0, and if T i = D i , the model can be further simplified to 〈T i , p i (j), a i (j)〉 k ∈ ℤ > 0, so we further define periodic task variable workload.

Definition 3 primary-alternate variable workload Given the periodic task set Γ = {τ 1 , τ 2 , ⋯ , τ n } , in a period, p i (j) ∈ p i b , p i w , a i (j) ∈ a i b , a i w are respectively defined as primary and alternate variable workload of task τ i in j-th release, where p i w , a i w respectively denote the WCET of primary and alternate, and p i b ,a i b respectively denote the BCET of primary and alternate.

div.p: A. Conventional periodic task primary-alternate faulttolerant scheduling algorithm 1) Scheduling objective a) Ensure that all tasks can be scheduled for the task set, i.e., the deadline of each cycle of each task is met; b) As much as possible to perform the primary, in order to achieve the higher quality results than alternate.
2) Scheduling Algorithm BCE algorithm mainly represents the conventional algorithm, and the basic idea is as follows.

a) Basic algorithm Basic algorithm firstly pre-establish a schedule of alternate in a planning period T using backwards-RM algorithm that is same with the RM algorithm except of one different point, backwards-RM algorithm schedule alternate from ending to beginning epoch in a planning cycle, i.e., the ending epoch is used as release time, and 0 epoch is used as ending epoch. According to Liu and Layland [6] evidence, RM algorithm is an optimal algorithm for static priority, therefore, for the alternate scheduling, backwards-RM is an optimal algorithm for static priority scheduling algorithm. After completing alternate's pre-assignment, in order to achieve as much as possible the execution of the primary, primary should be scheduled by Basic algorithm from front to back using the RM or EDF (Earliest-Deadline-First) algorithm, If the primary P i,j is successfully executed before the notification time, cancel corresponding alternate A i,j , and further adjust the affected other alternate's notification time; if primary P i,j execution fails, it must be terminated, and then alternate A i,j will be executed in notification time N i,j .

div.head: b) CAT algorithm
div.p: The basic idea of CAT algorithm is: in executing Basic algorithm, not only select the highest priority primary, but also calculate whether or not the available time is sufficient, and if there is not enough time, the primary will not be executed. CAT not only improves the primary success execution ratio, but also deduces the processor time waste due to the primary execution failure.

div.head: c) EIT algorithm
div.p: The basic idea of EIT algorithm is: at a scheduling epoch, if all the released task primary available execution times is insufficient and any notification time does not arrive, the processor is idle, execute the alternate of earliest notification time, in this way the idle time is eliminated, and further reduce the waste of processor time and further improve primary success execution ratio.

Because the task execution workload variables do not be considered, the execution time estimation value is larger than actual value in conventional periodic task primary-alternate fault-tolerant scheduling algorithm. In the scheduling process, except the task priority and deadline, task execution time is also a decisive influent factor for scheduling decisions, which directly causes primary not to be scheduled due to a conservative estimate of the execution time, and further affects the primary execution success ratio.
For example, in the CAT algorithm, the primary available time of task τ i in j-th release period can be calculated as
div.formula: AT ij (t) = N ij -t -∑ I i k i=1

But in fact, the probability that S i (t) equals to WCET is very small, so the result of CAT algorithm will not be right in the occasion, i.e., primary

div.p: Based on above analysis, we can draw the conclusion that primary-alternate fault-tolerant scheduling algorithm needs to be reanalyzed to solve conventional in considerable problem when task execution workload is variable.

div.head: B. Primary-alternate fault-tolerant scheduling analysis based on variable workload 1) Alternate scheduling analysis
div.p: During alternate scheduling, we should consider the following aspects of constraint. First, in order to ensure that all tasks deadline is met, the execution time a i (j) of alternate for each task must equal to its WCET, i.e., a i (j) = a i w . Second, alternate must be initiated by using off-line and preallocation policy, thus an idle time table including an integrity planning cycle can be provided before primary scheduling, which can decrease the difficulty of primary scheduling. Third, in order to maximize the success rate of the primary version of the implementation, we must ensure the implementation of the notification time for each subversion is the latest. In order to maximize the success rate of the primary, we must ensure the notification time for each alternate is the latest.

Conventional offline scheduling algorithm of single processor main includes RM algorithm of static priority and EDF algorithm of dynamic priority, where the sufficient condition of RM algorithm schedulability is processor utilization U ≤ n 2 1/n -1 and the sufficient and necessary condition of EDF algorithm schedulability is processor utilizationU ≤ 1. The schedulability of alternate is discussed in the following theorem 1.

Theorem 1: The sufficient and necessary condition of backwards-EDF algorithm schedulability is processor utilization U ≤ 1 in a single processor, periodicand preemptive task scheduling if alternate is deemed execution right.

Proof: backwards-EDF algorithm actually is EDF algorithm that only swap the release time and the deadline of each job, and because alternate execution is right, so the sufficient condition of backwards-EDF algorithm schedulability is processor utilization U ≤ 1 in a single processor, periodic, and preemptive task scheduling, and vice versa.

Example 1: The task set includes two tasks A〈5,3,2〉 and B〈7,5,4〉, respectively using backwards-RM and backwards-EDF algorithm to analyze the schedulability, and the result of scheduling is shown in Figure 2. We can deduce from figure 2: in the example, backwards-RM algorithm can't establish an alternate task schedule, but backwards-EDF algorithm do it. In the primary-alternate scheduling algorithm, whether or not establish an alternate task schedule is crucial, because it determines schedulability of a task set. Therefore, in the primary-alternate fault-tolerant scheduling algorithm, we select backwards-EDF algorithm rather than backwards-RM algorithm, because the former can significantly improve the schedulability of the task set.

2) Primary scheduling analysis Primary Scheduling can use RM algorithm, EDF algorithm and ENF (Earliest Notification time First) algorithm etc., where ENF algorithm can be seen as EDF algorithm that notification time equals the deadline.

Although the scheduling object of primary is periodic task set, after alternate schedule is pre-established, the primary scheduling, which differs from conventional scheduling using in periodic task set, emerges the following characteristics. a) Since the notification time is used theprimary deadline in each release period, the relative deadline of primary is less than its each job period and equal to the notification time.

b) The notification time is variable in the scheduling process, because after a primary is executed successfully, its corresponding alternate must be cancelled, furthermore,since alternate scheduling list of pre-allocation is created by preemption strategy, we need to re-adjust notification time of alternate that is broken by preemption. c) Theexecution time of primary ( ) is variable, and it is no longer equals to WCET, but its value is set between BCET and WCET.

div.head: C. Task error probability model of primary-alternate faulttolerant scheduling
div.p: One important objective of the primary-alternate faulttolerant scheduling is to improve the execution success ratio of primary. In the conventional primary-alternate faulttolerant scheduling policy, as long as the primary execution error occurs, the alternate must be executed to ensure task deadline to be met, so the primary must be dropped in the release cycle [1][2][3][4][14][15][16][17] , moreover, the failure due to primary error is not calculated in statistics metric of execution success ratio of primary because the error is regarded irrelevant to the scheduling policy. There are some problems about above assumption that should be discussed as following: First, execution success ratio of primary should be calculated on the statistics of primary execution error, because the definition of execution success ratio of primary is a ratio between the number of primary jobs and total jobs in a planning cycle. Second, the conventional algorithm assumes that the error occurring epoch is a time in which a job is executed after the last slice of WCET, if in this epoch the output of primary is unacceptable, the primary is regarded as error and will be dropped from execution queue, but in fact, on the one hand, the error epoch may occur during the entire cycle from release to deadline, on the other hand, even if the primary execution WCET is due, the primary can be executed until the processor time runs out in the cycle of the primary release, and the assumption is reasonable and can improve the execution success ratio of primary in the primary-alternate fault-tolerant scheduling.

There are several classifications in software faults of realtime systems [18] . We proposed an error probability model of primary-alternate fault-tolerant scheduling, shown in Figure 6. Figure 6 shows the error probability model of task τ i within the j-th cycle of job p ij , where t, p i b , p i (j), p i w , N ij is a vector and its item denotes scheduling decision time, BCET, non-error time of primary, WCET and notification time respectively. Error type of task can be divided into two classes, one is the IRIS error class that the primary has been executed until WCET is due and fails, but the primary may be executed for more time and be completed before deadline, and the other is non-IRIS error class that the output is not any reward for primary when error occurs, so the primary of job must be reset and re-executed.

Let stochastic ξ denotes the time of error occurring, and the probability distribution of ξ is t t+1 … q 1 q 2 … N ij q m where m = N ijt + 1 . Let q denotes the error probability of primary of task τ i , then ∑ q i = m i=1 q, and in equal probability condition, q i = q/(N ijt + 1). Let q IRIS denotes the probability of error in IRIS type when the occurring of error is inevitable, then the condition probability of IRIS type error is q × q IRIS /(N ijt + 1), and obviously that of non-IRIS type error is q × (1q IRIS )/(N ijt + 1).

div.head: IV. ALGORITHM OF BCE WITH VARIABLE WORKLOAD
div.p: Considering the performance of BCE and the influence of the variable workload on BCE, BCEVW (BCE with Variable Workload) algorithm is proposed. The following is a detailed description of the algorithm.

div.head: .T]: a timelist of task execution in a planning cycles,includingthe execution of the primary and the alternate version. d) DeadlineList[1 ..N]: a time list of the deadline for each task in the the current releasing cycle e) PrimaryList[1 ..N]: a list of execution time of the primary version for each task in the current releasingcycle f) AlternateList[1 ..N]: a list of execution time of the alternate version for each task in the current releasing cycle 2) Operating procedure& step
div.p: Step 1: Calculate the planning cycles T of the given tasks set and processor utilization of the alternate; if it meets the requirements of Condition 1and Condition 2 in the Theorem 3 (sect. III), apply the EDF algorithm to the alternate version scheduling according to Theorem 1(sect. III), and abandon the primary version scheduling, otherwise, execute the allocation algorithm of the alternate version for the task in Step 2.

Step 2: According to the conclusion of Theorem 1 (sect. III), pre-allocate time of the processor for the alternate version via the backwards-EDF algorithm that starts from the current moment t = T, finally, generate the reserved time sequence of alternate version. The specific process is as follows: Step 2.1 and 2.2.

Step 2.1: In the initialization AlternateList each element equal to zero and in the initialization DeadlineList each element equal to the beginning moment of the last cycle in a certain planning cycles.

Step 2.2: Establish the ExecutionList for the alternate version according to the time from the back to front in a planning cycles. Due to the strategy of backwards-EDF, the highest priority of execution is given to a task that is released in the latest moment. If the task is executed successfully within the period, set the corresponding element of the current task in the AlternateList as zero and set corresponding element in the DeadlineList as the releasing epoch in the previous cycle, then advance t to the next moment; if the task fails to be executed in a cycle, the preallocation of the alternate version fails and the algorithm ends.

Step 3: according to Theorem 4, calculate the feasibility of successful execution of all primary versions in task set Γ, and drop all unfeasible tasks fromΓto get a task sub-set Γ'. Starting from the current time t = 0, on the basis of EDF, schedule the primary versions of Γ' from front to back according to execution time, the detailed execution procedure is as follows from Step 3.1 to 3.7.
Step 3.1: Let each element in PrimaryList and AlternateList equal to zero in initialization, and each element inDeadlineList is the corresponding deadline of the first job of each task.

Step 3.2: From front to back in a planning period, establish the ExecuteList of the primary version. At the current time t, if the notification time of a task's alternate version is met, execute the alternate version of the task and reset the corresponding element to equal to zero in PrimaryList; and then determine whether the alternate version of the task has been completed, If completed, reset the corresponding element to equal to zero in AlternateList; then set the corresponding element in the deadlineList to equal to the deadline of the next cycle, and finally advance current time to the next moment t.
Step 3.3: At the current time t, if the notification time of the task isn't due, determine whether or not there are released task, if no, advance current time to the next moment.

Step 3.4: If there are released tasks in current time t, calculate the available time of all released tasks, and if available time is enough, select the earliest deadline of task in the task set of successful CAT calculation by EDF algorithm, and update the PrimaryList and ExecuteList, and if the primary version of the job is not completed, advance to the next time t, otherwise go to Step 3.5. If the CAT calculation of all released tasks fails, then go to Step 3.6.

Step 3.5: If the primary version of the task has been completed in the current release cycle, drop the corresponding pre-allocated alternate version of the task according to the Basic algorithm. The specific process is as follow: first, traversing the time interval from deadline of currently completed task to time t+1 backward, adjust the alternate that is preempted by currently completed job during the pre-allocation according to the backwards-EDF algorithm, finally, reset the corresponding element to equal to zero in PrimaryList and the corresponding element in the deadlineList to equal to the deadline of the next cycle, then advance current time to the next time t.

Step 3.6: In pre-allocated ExecuteList, search the task with the earliest notification time that has been released from the current time t to the ending time of planning period of current task set, if the search fails, the algorithm ends, else if the search is successful, execute the alternate version of the task in advance at the current time t and accumulate the corresponding element value of the AlternateList; if the execution of the alternate version ends, reset the corresponding element to equal to zero in AlternateList and the corresponding element in the deadlineList to equal to the deadline of the next cycle, and then advance current time to the next time t.
Step 3.7: if t = T, the algorithm ends, or else, returns to Step 3.2 and continues to schedule the primary version.

div.head: B. Results of simulation 1) Selection of the metrics
div.p: The main objective of the primary-alternate fault-tolerant scheduling algorithm is to get the maximum execution success ratio of the primary, therefore, two metrics are set to judge the ability of the scheduling algorithm: a) the schedulability of the task set b) execution success ratio of the primary The schedulability of the task set is regarded as the first metric, because if the pre-allocation of alternate fails, the task set can't be scheduled, however, the metric is often ignored. In the case that task set can be scheduled successfully, it is necessary to further analyze the second metric, i.e. execution success ratio of the primary.

div.head: VI. CONCLUSION
div.p: Compared with the analysis of the conventional WCET model, the scheduling of the primary-alternate based on the variable workload model is more complex, but it is more suitable for the real-time system. In this paper, the faulttolerant scheduling of periodic tasks in primary-alternate is studied on the basis of the analysis of variable workload model, and not only the scheduling theorem of the alternate version, but also the theorem of the primary version in the critical state of the workload are proved. Moreover, Aiming at the problems existing in the research of task error probability distribution in the conventional fault-tolerance model, a novel task error probability model that takes the different task errors in different errors epoch into account. On the basis of theoretical research the BCE algorithm, BCEVW is proposed by above scheduling theorems. To further verify the correctness of the theory and algorithm performance, random task sets are generated by Monte Carlo, in which the random of simulation obey uniform distribution. The conventional algorithm and the novel algorithm are simulated by the metrics that comprise the schedulability of the task set and the execution success ratio of the primary version. The results show that: (1) The simulation result is in complete accordance with the theoretical argument; (2) BCEVW is superior to the conventional algorithm in the two metrics; (3) On the defined error probability model, the results of scheduling of BCEVW algorithm show there is a significant linear relationship between error probability and the execution success ratio of the primary version.
